headline: Sequence language models now predict RNA modifications and ribosome profiling coverage
label: Learned Sequence Representations
synthesis: The common thread is machine learning applied directly to sequence or read-level data, with biological context added to the prediction. EvoRMD couples an evolutionary RNA language model with species, tissue, cell-type and localization metadata to predict eleven RNA modification types jointly. RiboPipe imputes codon-resolution Ribo-seq coverage for low-coverage transcripts by jointly modelling transcript-level mean ribosome load with codon-resolution coverage. MEIsensor applies deep learning to HiFi long-read data to detect and classify Alu, LINE1 and SVA insertions. MPore takes a different route, combining REBASE homology search with regularized logistic regression to identify active methyltransferases and their target motifs from Nanopore R10 reads. What is new is explicit biological structure entering the model, most clearly as metadata conditioning in EvoRMD and as a transcript-level hierarchy in RiboPipe.
